label: closed-book
what: at every site of the probe design s2b, which bit of configuration memory is which cell of its LUT RAM: found by writing the RAM at every site at once through user logic and reading configuration memory back, the site of a place from the word its memory was loaded with (docs/s2_plan.md, sections 45 and 46). An address is the frame address the device named, a word of the frame read there (0 the first) and a bit of that word (0 the least significant).
numbering: site: the design's number for a site; its name is the design's record of where the build placed the memories it loaded with the words found there. cell = 64 x memory + ram_address. memory: which bit of the design's data register writes it (0 to 3). ram_address: what the design's address register held (0 to 63). Which LUT of a slice a memory is, and which pin carries which address bit, is not shown by this.

confidence.0: contradiction: with that cell alone set at every site, the bits that changed are not the places decoded for it
confidence.1: decoded from the code states and the loaded words only
confidence.2: confirmed: with that cell alone set at every site, exactly the places decoded for it, one a site, read otherwise than the base

evidence.the_site: which site an entry is of rests on the runs of part 1 and on them alone: the word the design loads a memory with was found in the frames read there before anything was written, at the entry's place. The runs of part 2 write every site alike and show nothing of it; a single confirms the cell of a place, not its site.
evidence.what: every site was written alike, so what an entry rests on is said once for each cell: the states of the code run in which the cell was one, and the run and state of the singles in which it alone was. The record of a run in which a place's frame was read in a state is 2 + state x (number of reads) + (the read that delivers the frame); the reads are the same in every run of part 2.
